dissents.topic: Severity of the Close vs CloseStream message-name mismatch

positions.position: P0 — this is the load-bearing fact of the PR; if wrong, the patch does not fix what it claims and must not land.
P1 — the wait-for-ack invariant does not hold if the server does not recognize 'Close'; needs verification against Speak v1 protocol.
P1 — the value being sent is the load-bearing fact and must match the protocol.
P1 — precondition mismatch at the protocol boundary; the constant should be CloseStream.
P1 — possible wrong-string bug; verify which token Speak v1 actually expects before merging.
P1 — UNREASONED contradiction between cited spec and code; refuse in current form.

dissents.topic: Whether _close_ws should drain until a terminal close-frame or whether one receive() suffices

positions.position: Either drain until a typed Close-ack frame (bounded by a deadline) or document precisely why a single frame suffices.
The drain should be a named step that reads until a terminal message or timeout, not a one-shot receive(); one-shot is a guess, not a protocol.
Single ws.receive() with 1s timeout is cargo-cult synchronization and the comment is a lie; need a loop reading until close ack.
The drain loop should read until a Close/Closed frame or timeout; in-flight audio handling should be in the postcondition.
A small loop reading until a close/ack frame or timeout would match the stated intent more honestly, but tone is lighter — it's a P2 nit.
TESTED-NOT-PROVED — either drain until close-frame with stated invariant or do not pretend to wait at all.

dissents.topic: Whether sending Flush alongside Close is justified

positions.position: Two patches in one — Flush is not part of the stated fix; either justify it in the commit message or drop it (P2).
Flush is unjustified by the stated specification; semantics during teardown not analyzed (P2).
Treats Flush+Close as a unit without objecting to its inclusion; concerns are about the drain semantics, not Flush itself.
No objection to Flush specifically; concern is the complecting of protocol shutdown with drain and transport close.

issues.description: Close control message uses {"type":"Close"} but PR description and Deepgram docs specify {"type":"CloseStream"}
issues.detail: Every reviewer flagged this as the load-bearing issue of the PR. The PR title, description, and linked Deepgram references all state the required control message is {"type":"CloseStream"}, but _CLOSE_MSG is json.dumps({"type":"Close"}). Torvalds rates it P0 because if Deepgram requires CloseStream the patch fixes nothing; the other five rate it P1 but agree it must be reconciled against the live Speak v1 protocol before merge. The wait-for-ack invariant the PR claims to establish cannot hold if the server does not recognize the message it receives.

issues.description: Single ws.receive() with 1s timeout does not establish a server-acknowledgment postcondition
issues.detail: Five reviewers independently noted that ws.receive() returns the next frame of any kind — likely an in-flight audio chunk or metadata frame, not the close acknowledgment — so treating any-frame-received as 'cleanly closed' is best-effort dressed up as a termination proof. The comment claiming this prevents 429s from lingering sessions overstates what the code does. Recommended fix: drain in a loop until a Close/Closed frame or deadline, or explicitly document that this is best-effort with residual 429 risk.

issues.description: Bare `except Exception` in _close_ws swallows distinguishable failure modes including CancelledError
issues.detail: Torvalds, Liskov, and Dijkstra rate this P1; Knuth and Pike rate it P2. The catch collapses already-closed-socket (expected), ConnectionResetError, aiohttp.ClientError, programmer errors, and asyncio.CancelledError into one warning. Dijkstra and Liskov both insist CancelledError must be re-raised so cooperative cancellation during shutdown is not silently swallowed. The fix is to narrow the except to the specific aiohttp/connection errors actually expected on the close path.

issues.description: _close_ws complects protocol shutdown, drain/race-waiting, and transport close in one method
issues.detail: Hickey frames this as the central design issue: three separable concerns (sending Flush+Close, waiting on receive as a proxy for 'server caught up', and closing the transport) are fused in one method with no named drain step. Each has different failure modes and time semantics, and the implicit loop hides what invariant is being established. Refactor into a named drain step plus a close step so the protocol contract is observable.

issues.description: PR bundles unrelated behavior changes — Flush-on-close is not justified by the stated fix
issues.detail: Torvalds and Dijkstra both note that the commit message argues only for CloseStream but the diff additionally sends Flush. Deepgram's Speak protocol distinguishes Flush (force-render current buffer) from Close (end session); during teardown Flush is either redundant or changes audio-output semantics for in-flight synthesis. The author has not stated which, and Torvalds calls it 'THREE-PATCHES territory' (constant rename, Flush-on-close, drain-before-close).

issues.description: Ordering of the two send_str calls is not analyzed — Flush failure aborts Close transmission
issues.detail: If the first send_str (Flush) raises because the peer already closed, the second send_str (Close) is skipped and control jumps to the broad except, so the postcondition 'Close was transmitted' is not established on the very failure mode the catch exists to hide. Either send Close first, wrap each in independent try-blocks, or explicitly document best-effort.

issues.description: Magic 1.0s timeout has no name, no derivation, and silent TimeoutError loses diagnostic signal
issues.detail: Hickey, Dijkstra, and Knuth all note the 1.0 second budget is essential behavior — how long we wait for Deepgram to drain — but is inlined as a literal with no justification for why one second is sufficient. The swallowed TimeoutError loses the exact diagnostic operators would need when 429s recur. Recommended: pull out as a named constant or conn_option and at least log at debug on timeout.

issues.description: Comment overstates what the code guarantees — claims 'race condition / 429 prevention' that the implementation does not establish
issues.detail: Knuth and Torvalds (and implicitly Pike, Dijkstra) note the comment claims the wait prevents race conditions and 429s from lingering sessions, but with a one-shot receive and silently-swallowed TimeoutError the code provides at-best best-effort. A literate comment should state the actual invariant: 'best-effort drain up to 1s; on timeout we proceed with close and accept residual 429 risk.'

issues.description: _FLUSH_MSG / _CLOSE_MSG live on SynthesizeStream but are read from a method on the outer (TTS/ChunkedStream) class
issues.detail: Four reviewers (Knuth, Hickey, Liskov, Pike) flagged the cross-class reach. Hickey and Liskov go further: the Deepgram wire-protocol control messages are an abstract data type of their own and should be a module-level shared vocabulary (or small ControlMessage type), ideally colocated with the STT side that already gets this right. Hickey notes two copies of the same protocol data in two files is incidental duplication waiting to drift — and this PR is itself evidence of that drift (Close vs CloseStream).

issues.description: f-string formatting used in logger.warning call instead of lazy %-formatting
issues.detail: logger.warning(f"...{e}") formats the string even when the level filters it out. Use logger.warning("Error during WebSocket close sequence: %s", e). Minor and stylistic but it's the broader Python logging convention.

issues.description: No test asserts the exact JSON wire-payload sent on close
issues.detail: Dijkstra notes that _FLUSH_MSG / _CLOSE_MSG are computed at import time and there is no unit test asserting the chosen 'Close' vs 'CloseStream' matches the cited SDK reference. The absence of such a test is itself the bug under the bug: a single assertEqual on the JSON payload would have caught the Close/CloseStream contradiction before review.

synthesis.summary: All six reviewers converge on a single load-bearing finding: the PR description and Deepgram documentation say the close control message is {"type":"CloseStream"}, but the code sends {"type":"Close"} — Torvalds rates this P0 ("doesn't fix what it claims to fix"), the other five rate it P1 but agree it must be reconciled against the live Speak v1 protocol (and Pike notes Speak v1 vs Listen v1 use different names) before merge. The next strongest claim, raised by all six, is that the single ws.receive() with a 1s timeout does not establish the server-acknowledgment postcondition the comment advertises — it returns whatever frame is next (likely in-flight audio), so the patch narrows the race rather than closing it; reviewers split on whether the fix is to drain in a loop or to honestly document best-effort. The strongest preserved disagreement is on severity of the Close-vs-CloseStream mismatch (Torvalds P0, everyone else P1) and on whether bundling Flush into this patch is acceptable (Torvalds and Dijkstra object explicitly; others are silent or accept it as part of the shutdown sequence). Secondary unanimous concerns: the bare except Exception swallows CancelledError and benign already-closed conditions identically, the protocol-vocabulary constants reach across class boundaries and should be a shared ADT, and there is no test asserting the exact JSON payload — Dijkstra notes such a test would have caught this bug under the bug.
